supporting_observations.claim: During the alert window, WS-MFISCHER-01 had multiple connections to the explicit proxy at 10.55.20.30:8080. Zeek records show HTTP service and recurring traffic volumes, including about 10 KB sent and 39 KB received in several connections.

The available records for those connections show client-to-proxy traffic, but do not identify the HTTPS destination or the endpoint process responsible; they therefore do not establish whether the traffic was the approved LedgerLink updater or another application.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records for the alert-period connections are Zeek connections to the proxy, not proxy CONNECT/GET records identifying the external destinations.
The supplied alert-period connection records do not include a process ID or executable attribution.
The listed connection records do not independently establish the alert's reported roughly five-minute cadence; the evidence may be incomplete for that interval.
claims_not_established: Whether the alerted connections reached update.ledgerlink.com or another destination.
Whether ledgerlinkupd.exe, another approved application, or an unapproved process generated the connections.
Whether the periodic connections carried malicious content or data.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve PROXY-SUN-01 CONNECT and, where available, inspected request records for WS-MFISCHER-01 from 13:20 to 14:20 UTC, including destination hostnames, tunnel IDs, byte counts, and timestamps.
Correlate each proxy connection with endpoint process/network telemetry and identify the executable path, signature, and hash.
Review endpoint DNS and TLS/SNI or certificate telemetry for the destinations contacted during the alert window.
Verify whether LedgerLink and its updater were installed and running on WS-MFISCHER-01 at the time.
unrelated_findings: Before the alert window, max.fischer launched an encoded PowerShell command that decodes to a query for stopped services; the same session also launched WMIC to list running services. Review separately; these records do not identify the process behind the alerted proxy connections. (T236-00131, T236-00132, T236-00020, T236-00024, T236-00029)

Before the alert window, max.fischer launched psql.exe with the postgres account against the metrics and appdata databases from cmd.exe. Review separately; these records do not establish a connection to the alerted activity. (T236-00071, T236-00073, T236-00074, T236-00079)

At 14:17 UTC, PROXY-SUN-01 connected to WS-MFISCHER-01 on TCP port 135, with endpoint records attributing the connection to svchost.exe running as SYSTEM. This is separate from the outbound proxy connections in the alert and merits separate review. (T236-00374, T236-00375, T236-00376, T236-00377)
